title: Crypto, from the math up
subtitle: What hashing, keys and chains actually do - not what the metaphors say.
description: Every explanation of blockchain reaches for a metaphor: a ledger, a chain, a village of accountants. This course skips them. One payment - 0.05 BTC for a vintage synthesiser - runs through the first half of the course, and every mechanism arrives because that payment needs it. You will see the actual machinery, one screen at a time, including the parts that have failed in public.

lessons.title: What a hash actually does
lessons.summary: One-way, fixed-size, wildly sensitive - and why that is enough to build a chain.

lessons.title: Committing to a secret
lessons.summary: How to prove what you decided without saying what it was - and the salt that stops the trick collapsing.

lessons.title: Where a key comes from
lessons.summary: A private key is 256 random bits. Everything rests on the word random, and that word has failed in production.

lessons.title: The one-way street
lessons.summary: Multiplying a point on a curve is easy. Dividing is not. That asymmetry is the whole public-key idea.

lessons.title: What a signature proves
lessons.summary: Two numbers, r and s, and a verification that never sees the private key - nor, importantly, the signer.

lessons.title: The number that leaked a console
lessons.summary: Sony signed twice with the same nonce. Two signatures, three lines of algebra, one recovered master key.

lessons.title: From a key to an address
lessons.summary: Hash, hash again, add a checksum: why a mistyped address bounces instead of burning your money.

chapters.title: Making a ledger out of it

lessons.title: There are no balances
lessons.summary: Your wallet holds coins the way a pocket holds notes: indivisible, spent whole, with change handed back.

lessons.title: What the signature covers
lessons.summary: A signature that did not commit to the outputs would be a blank cheque. Sighash is the fine print.

lessons.title: Proving membership
lessons.summary: A Merkle tree lets a phone verify one transaction out of four thousand by downloading twelve hashes.

lessons.title: Eighty bytes
lessons.summary: A block header is smaller than this sentence's worth of text, and it is the only part most of the network checks.

lessons.title: Tamper-evident is not tamper-proof
lessons.summary: The chain tells you the history changed. It does not stop anyone changing it - that is a different job entirely.

lessons.title: The only hard problem
lessons.summary: Copying money is trivially detectable. Ordering two conflicting spends, with no clock and no referee, is not.

lessons.title: What the puzzle actually is
lessons.summary: Miners are not solving anything. They are counting, and the target says how low the answer must land.

lessons.title: The thermostat
lessons.summary: Every 2016 blocks the network re-reads its own clock and changes the difficulty. The clamp matters more than the formula.

lessons.title: Nothing is ever final
lessons.summary: Confirmations are not a countdown to certainty. They are a probability curve, and you can read it.

lessons.title: Fifty-one percent
lessons.summary: What a majority of hashpower can actually do to you - and the far shorter list of what it cannot.

lessons.title: Staking instead
lessons.summary: Ethereum swapped electricity for collateral in one block. What that bought, and what it cost.

lessons.title: Money with conditions
lessons.summary: Bitcoin outputs are locked by a small stack program. Multisig and timelocks are just two ways of writing it.

lessons.title: Two ways to model the world
lessons.summary: UTXOs versus accounts: the same money, two data structures, and very different failure modes.

lessons.title: The DAO and the order of two lines
lessons.summary: Reentrancy is not an exotic bug. It is sending the money before you write down that you sent it.

lessons.title: A token is a mapping
lessons.summary: There is no coin. There is a table of numbers in one contract, and a rule about who may change it.

lessons.title: Pseudonymous is not anonymous
lessons.summary: Every payment you ever made is public forever. Two heuristics turn that into a name.

lessons.title: Twelve words
lessons.summary: A seed phrase is not a password. It is your entire key space, compressed into a checksum-protected sentence.

lessons.title: The auction you are in
lessons.summary: Block space is a fixed supply sold continuously. Your fee is a bid, and bots can see it.

lessons.title: The weakest link is the bridge
lessons.summary: The biggest thefts in the field share one shape: the chain held, and the thing beside it did not.

lessons.title: What it cannot do
lessons.summary: A chain can guarantee a number was not changed. It can never guarantee the number was true.
